competition.title: Battle Day: What to Expect
competition.intro: Battle of the Books is a reading tournament. Mesa Academy's Knights compete against other Arizona schools in three battles during the year, and the scores from all three add up.

sections.title: Your team
points: Teams have two or three students.
Talk it over! Teammates are supposed to discuss answers and use their time well.
One person is the spokesperson. They sit in the middle and give the team's answer.

sections.title: Phase I: “In which book…?” (5 rounds)
points: You hear a clue, then answer with the book's title and author.
You have 30 seconds to talk it over.
Correct title = 5 points. Correct author = 3 more points.
The author only counts if the title is right, so the title matters most!
Example style: “In which book did a spider spin words into a web?”

sections.title: Phase II: short facts (3 rounds)
points: These questions name the book and ask a short, factual question about it.
You have 20 seconds.
A correct answer = 10 points. There are no bonus points.
Example style: “In Where the Red Fern Grows, what were the names of the dogs?”

sections.title: The clock
points: The timer starts as soon as the question has been read.
You'll hear a five-second warning.
When time is called, no more answers, unless your spokesperson has already started. “Um…” and “Uh…” don't count as starting!
You can ask to hear the question again, but the clock keeps running while it's re-read.
If the judges ask you to be more specific, you get 10 more seconds.

sections.title: Titles and authors
points: Say the title exactly, including little words like “The”.
For the author, the last name alone is fine. A wrong first name with the right last name still counts.
Close-enough pronunciation of the author's last name is OK.

sections.title: Always guess
points: Wrong answers never lose points, so always give an answer.
At school battles, the questioner only says “Correct” or “Incorrect”. They won't tell you the right answer, and the question isn't passed to another team.

sections.title: Challenges and judges
points: If your answer is a little different from the written one, the judges decide.
If you're sure you were right, your team can challenge, but only before the next team's question starts.
For a challenge, the judges look in the book and your team gets 3 minutes to find the proof.
The judges' decision is final.

sections.title: Be a good Knight
points: Be on your best behavior. Talking out of turn or poor sportsmanship can get a team disqualified.
Be on time. A battle waits at most five minutes, and missed rounds can't be made up.

sections.title: How the season works
points: Scores from Battles 1, 2 and 3 are added together.
Each school sends its top-scoring team to the District Semi-finals in April.
The top four teams from each semi-final go on to the MPS District Final.
The top three teams at the District Final go to the Regional Battle on May 5.
Ties are broken with extra Phase II questions until one team misses and another gets theirs right.

tips: Memorize every title and the author's last name. It's the easiest way to earn points.
Practice saying titles exactly, little words included.
Pick your spokesperson before the battle, and agree on how you'll decide when you disagree.
Watch the clock. Settle on an answer before the five-second warning.
Not sure? Guess anyway. A guess can't cost you points.

factSheet.oneLiner: A 12-year-old criminal genius kidnaps a fairy police officer to get a ransom of fairy gold.
factSheet.summary: Artemis Fowl II is a 12-year-old genius from an Irish family of criminals. His father has disappeared and the family fortune is gone, so Artemis makes a bold plan: steal the secrets of the fairies, kidnap one, and demand gold as ransom. He captures Captain Holly Short of the fairy police (the LEP). The fairies surround his home, Fowl Manor, freeze time around it, and try everything to rescue her — but Artemis has a plan for almost everything.

characters.desc: 12-year-old genius and heir to a criminal family; wants fairy gold to rebuild the family fortune.

characters.desc: A kleptomaniac dwarf criminal who tunnels by eating dirt; sent to break into Fowl Manor.

characters.desc: A fairy in Ho Chi Minh City with a drinking problem; Artemis gets her Book and gives her a cure.

characters.name: Dr. J. Argon

keyObjects.desc: The fairies' secret rulebook, written in Gnommish. Artemis translates it with computer software.

keyObjects.desc: Butler uses it to capture Holly.

keyObjects.desc: Artemis's trick for slipping out of the time-stop.

keyObjects.name: Foaly's tinfoil hat
keyObjects.desc: Worn to block imagined spying.

themes.name: Brains vs. brawn
themes.desc: Artemis wins with planning and cleverness, while others rely on strength or magic.

themes.name: Family
themes.desc: Behind the crime, Artemis is trying to save his broken family: his missing father and sick mother.

themes.name: Good guys and bad guys
themes.desc: The 'villain' is the main character, and both sides do good and bad things.

themes.name: Magic vs. technology
themes.desc: Fairy magic goes up against human gadgets, and Foaly's science matches Artemis's.

themes.name: Humans and nature
themes.desc: The fairies hid underground to get away from humans, who harm the Earth.

outline.title: The Book
outline.summary: Artemis (age 12) and Butler go to Ho Chi Minh City. Their contact, Nguyen, leads them to a fairy healer. Artemis gets her Book of the People and gives her a shot that cures her drinking. Back at Fowl Manor in Ireland, Artemis translates the Gnommish Book. His father is missing after a shipping disaster, and his mother stays shut in her room.

outline.title: Holly and the Abduction
outline.summary: Captain Holly Short of LEP Recon is sent after a troll that has escaped to the surface. She saves the humans, but it uses up her magic. Commander Root orders her to do the Ritual, so she goes to Ireland. Artemis and Butler have been watching the likely Ritual sites. Butler hits her with a tranquilizer dart while she's renewing her magic, and they take her back to Fowl Manor.

outline.title: Missing in Action / Siege
outline.summary: The LEP realizes Holly has been kidnapped. Root follows her locator beacon to a whaling ship, but Artemis planted it there with a bomb, and Root barely escapes. Holly wakes at Fowl Manor, and Artemis tricks her into thinking she spilled fairy secrets under truth serum. The LEP surrounds the manor, and Butler beats the officers they send in. The fairies start a time-stop, and Artemis demands one ton of gold, saying he knows how to escape the time-stop.

outline.title: Mulch and the Troll
outline.summary: Root sends Mulch Diggums, a dwarf thief who can enter houses uninvited, to tunnel in. Mulch finds Artemis's copy of the Book, then fakes his own death and escapes. Holly breaks her cell floor, finds soil, and does the Ritual to get her magic back. Cudgeon takes over and sends a troll into the manor. Butler nearly dies, but Holly heals him and he defeats the troll. Root is put back in charge.

outline.title: The Escape
outline.summary: The fairies hand over the gold. Holly takes half of it back in exchange for granting Artemis a wish. Artemis, Butler, and Juliet drink sedative-laced champagne. The fairies set off the blue rinse, but when they try to enter, they get sick, which proves Artemis is alive. By falling asleep, the humans slipped out of the time-stop. The fairies leave, and Artemis's wish comes true: his mother is healed. The epilogue shows the story is Dr. Argon's case file.

factSheet.oneLiner: The family dog tells how the family cat became sure their new pet bunny was a vampire.
factSheet.summary: Harold, the Monroe family's dog, tells the story. The Monroes find a small rabbit at a movie theater while watching Dracula and bring him home. Chester the cat reads lots of horror books, and he decides the bunny, Bunnicula, is a vampire: he sleeps all day, has fangs, and vegetables start turning white. Chester tries garlic, a 'steak' through the heart, and more to stop him, until everything ends in chaos and a trip to the vet.

characters.desc: The easygoing, snack-loving family dog who tells the story.

themes.name: Jumping to conclusions
themes.desc: Chester's imagination runs wild, and his 'evidence' leads him to do silly and harmful things.

themes.name: Friendship
themes.desc: Harold and Chester's friendship is tested when they disagree about the bunny.

themes.name: Jealousy of the new arrival
themes.desc: The vet says Chester's trouble is a kind of sibling rivalry with the new pet.

themes.name: Kindness to someone different
themes.desc: Harold chooses to help the strange little bunny instead of fearing him.

outline.title: The Arrival
outline.summary: The book is presented as a manuscript written by a dog. On a dark and stormy night, the Monroes find a tiny bunny with a note at a showing of Dracula. Mrs. Monroe names him Bunnicula.

outline.title: Suspicion
outline.summary: Pete and Toby fight over caring for the bunny, and Harold feels left out. Chester notices that the bunny's markings look like a cape and that he sleeps all day. Using his books, Chester begins to suspect a vampire.

outline.title: The White Vegetables
outline.summary: Chester tells Harold that Bunnicula has been getting out of his cage. Mr. Monroe finds the first drained vegetable, a white tomato. Later, Harold joins Chester's night watch. They see Bunnicula leaving the kitchen and find a white zucchini, and Harold starts taking Chester's vampire idea more seriously.

outline.title: Chester Takes Action
outline.summary: More vegetables turn white, and Chester tries and fails to warn the Monroes that Bunnicula is a vampire. He puts garlic around the bunny's cage and gets a bath for smelling of it. Then he mixes up 'stake' and 'steak' and attacks Bunnicula with a raw steak. Finally he tries water, and his behavior gets him shut outside.

outline.title: Starvation, Salad, and the Vet
outline.summary: Harold figures out that Chester is keeping Bunnicula away from food on purpose, and the bunny grows weak. Harold brings Bunnicula to the salad, Chester attacks, and the dinner table turns to chaos. The family takes the pets to the vet. The vet gives Bunnicula carrot juice, and Chester starts seeing a cat psychiatrist.

factSheet.oneLiner: After his football-star brother falls into a coma, a 10-year-old boy becomes a homemade superhero.
factSheet.summary: Newt Newman is a quiet 10-year-old who feels invisible next to his big brother Chris, the star quarterback in their town of Appleton. When Chris is knocked into a coma during the Big Game, Newt's friends Cecil and JJ help him turn Chris's old football clothes into a Halloween costume, and Captain Nobody is born. Newt keeps wearing it and finds the courage to help people, stop a robbery, and learn the truth about his brother's accident.

themes.desc: Newt can save strangers but feels he can't save his own brother.

themes.name: Friendship

outline.title: Falling
outline.summary: Newt is falling from Appleton's water tower. As he falls, he remembers how it all started on the morning of the Big Game.

outline.title: Nobody Eats Breakfast
outline.summary: On the last Friday in October, Newt makes breakfast, but his busy parents are always on the phone. The newspaper hypes Chris and the Big Game against Merrimac. Newt wakes Chris up with a yell and then sprays him with the garden hose.

outline.title: Inner Other and the Big Game
outline.summary: Newt, Cecil, and JJ agree to build Halloween costumes that show their 'inner other'. At the Big Game, Newt ends up outside the stadium and watches from behind a fence. Chris scores the winning touchdown but doesn't get up, and he's in a coma.

outline.title: Captain Nobody Is Born
outline.summary: On Halloween, Cecil and JJ turn Chris's old jersey and clothes into a superhero costume. Newt uses Chris's initials, C.N., to name himself Captain Nobody. He wears it to school, where kids tease him at first. He helps Cecil get a bass drum off a dumpster and then walks a lost Mr. Clay home.

outline.title: Hero Around Town
outline.summary: Ricky, Reggie's cousin, confronts Newt, and the class sticks up for Newt. JJ's complaint about the grammar on a sign takes Newt into Sullivan's Jewelry during a robbery, and the owner sets off the alarm. Newt finds a medical report saying Chris may never wake. The mascot ferret escapes onto the highway, and when Newt stops traffic, a small plane is able to make an emergency landing.

outline.title: The Water Tower
outline.summary: In a dream, Newt remembers that a teammate, Darryl, really caused Chris's injury. Reggie is on the water tower, and people fear the worst, but he's just stuck after trying to paint graffiti. Captain Nobody climbs up to help and falls, landing on a rubber mattress, and then Reggie lands on him. In the hospital, Newt tells the truth about the accident. When Newt visits Chris, Chris wakes up. Newt later leads the victory parade as Captain Nobody.

factSheet.oneLiner: A sixth-grade artist buys a strange sphere at a magic shop, and it hatches into a dragon only a few people can see.
factSheet.summary: Jeremy Thatcher loves to draw, but his art teacher, Mr. Kravitz, is always criticizing him. Running from bullies and from Mary Lou Hutton, who has a crush on him, Jeremy finds Elives' Magic Supplies and buys a colorful sphere for a quarter. It's a dragon egg. The baby dragon, Tiamat, hatches under the full moon, shares thoughts with Jeremy, and grows fast. Jeremy has to keep her secret, care for her, and finally send her home to the dragons' world on Midsummer Night.

settings.name: The school art room
settings.desc: Mr. Kravitz's class.

keyObjects.name: The instructions

keyObjects.desc: Jeremy must save them and later uses them to build the gate home.

keyObjects.desc: Jeremy is finally old enough for the top prize, painting a department-store window.

themes.name: Art and believing in yourself
themes.desc: Jeremy learns to trust his own talent even when a teacher puts it down.

themes.name: Responsibility
themes.desc: Caring for a fast-growing dragon is hard, tiring work.

themes.name: Love and letting go
themes.desc: Jeremy has to send Tiamat home because he loves her, and he learns that nothing you love is ever truly lost.

themes.name: Friendship
themes.desc: His friendship with Spess is tested, and a new one grows with Mary Lou.

themes.name: Honesty
themes.desc: Jeremy confesses to the fire prank so his classmates can enter the contest.

outline.title: Love Letter of Doom
outline.summary: Mr. Kravitz embarrasses Jeremy by reading Mary Lou's note aloud in art class. Jeremy and Spess talk about the spring art contest. Running from Mary Lou and the bullies Howard Morton and Freddy the Frog Killer, Jeremy finds Elives' Magic Supplies. Mr. Elives sells him a colorful sphere for a quarter, says the sphere chose him, and gives him strict instructions. Jeremy is magically sent home.

outline.title: Hatching
outline.summary: The instructions explain how to hatch a dragon egg, with a spell said under a full moon, which Jeremy's dad says is tomorrow night. Jeremy says the spell, falls asleep in a lawn chair, and wakes to see the egg hatch. The instructions now say to feed her chicken livers, keep her secret, and save her skin, teeth, and eggshell. Miss Priest lends him a dragon book written by Mr. Elives. The dragon goes after his gerbils, and Jeremy realizes his mom can't see her.

outline.title: Tiamat · Still Life · The Dragon Who Came to Dinner
outline.summary: Milk puts the dragon to sleep. She turns down names like Fafnir and Smaug until Jeremy tries Tiamat. Spess can't see her. The boys fail to find the shop again and argue, and the dragon book goes missing. Jeremy leaves school after sensing Tiamat's pain; she has shed her skin. Mary Lou follows him home and can see Tiamat. At the dinner with the Huttons, Tiamat chases the cats and Grief yanks off the tablecloth.

outline.title: The Heat Is On · The Hatchers · Confessions
outline.summary: Tiamat follows Jeremy to school through the cat door. When Mr. Kravitz insults fantasy art, she feels Jeremy's anger and breathes fire on the teacher's shoe. Kravitz bans the whole class from the art contest. Spess admits he took the dragon book. A letter from Mr. Elives says Tiamat must go home on Midsummer Night. Jeremy confesses, and Kravitz lets the class back in but still bans Jeremy.

outline.title: Night Flights · Nothing You Love Is Lost · Epilogue
outline.summary: Tiamat moves to the barn, and Mary Lou helps with milk. Jeremy rides on Tiamat's back at night. On Midsummer Night, Tiamat cries a diamond tear. At the magic shop, Jeremy and Miss Priest build a gate from her skin and teeth, and Tiamat goes home. Jeremy is sad all summer. At a Halloween party, his mind-link with Tiamat returns, Miss Priest shows she also has a dragon tear, and Jeremy starts drawing again.
